title: What If You Knew the Last Time You'd See Someone?
con: A counter reading 42 over your mother at the door will stop a thumb and then spoil ordinary evenings.
pro: The counter transforms ordinary family moments into suspense, grief and a memorable perspective on limited time.

title: What If You Got Paid Every Time Someone Thought of You?
con: Instantly checkable, funny, and lands on a melancholy truth about who really carries you.
pro: Turns social vanity and the psychological spotlight effect into an unforgettable emotional reveal about a mother's constant quiet love.

title: What If You Could Sell One Year of Your Life?
con: Hospital-bill stakes make the time-for-money trade painfully Indian and the keep-tapping escalation writes itself.
pro: Medical debt forcing a child to sell years of life is the most painfully Indian premise here.

title: What If You Could Step Into Any Photo for 5 Minutes?
con: Five minutes in a rain-and-tea photograph, with someone standing just outside the frame, is a film this medium can shoot.
pro: The five-minute rule, photographic boundaries and lost loved one create a cinematic story perfectly suited to layered paper sets.

title: What If You Saw Everyone's Real Odds of Success?
con: Odds glowing over a coaching hall speaks directly to the exam-generation viewer's deepest fear.
pro: A coaching-hall setting, glowing probability HUD, and self-fulfilling sibling twist hit the bullseye for exam-age Indian and global viewers alike.

title: What If You Could Fast-Forward the Boring Parts of Life?
con: Skipping family dinners on autopilot is a quiet horror the commute-weary viewer will feel.
pro: It begins with universal commute frustration and escalates into a chilling loss of continuity, memory and family presence.

title: What If You Could Hear Everything Said About You?
con: Gossip stats subvert paranoia nicely, though the escalation ceiling is modest.
pro: It taps a universal social anxiety, and the 'mostly neutral' gossip data is a surprising, comforting flip.

title: What If You Could Never Forget Anything?
con: Directly subverts the board-exam fantasy of photographic memory with the real science of HSAM trapping people in un-fading emotional hurts.
pro: The night before boards, perfect memory turns on the shouting from when you were nine and will not turn it off.

title: What If Everyone Could See Your Search History?
con: Every search floating over you on the metro, including the 2am boards search your mother reads, is public shame this viewer already fears.
pro: The 2 AM boards search floating above your head is the single most relatable exposure here.

title: What If Tomorrow Texted You Tonight?
con: A gripping thriller with a damned-either-way dilemma and a clever base-rate insight.
pro: The text about your mother's 8:10 bus is a whole thriller, and the false-alarm math keeps either choice dangerous.

title: What If You Could Save and Reload the Last 60 Seconds?
con: Snapping back the interview answer works until your father's heart attack sits two minutes before the save point.
pro: A natural follow-up to the channel's first video that pairs effortless loop-animation reuse with an unforgettable third-act twist about your father.

title: What If You Could Erase Someone From Your Mind?
con: A sharp neuroscience twist on Eternal Sunshine where deleting an ex unravels the associative memory network holding your late father's final voicemail.
pro: A seductive power becomes a devastating family loss, with clear escalation and unusually strong emotional stakes.

title: What If Everyone Forgot You for a Day?
con: A mother's polite chai greeting makes forgetting instantly heartbreaking, and the recognition science adds real depth.
pro: Your mother offering you guest-chai is the whole film, and familiarity failing while the face still matches makes it worse.

title: What If You Woke Up as Your Parent?
con: Body-swap with your father on exam morning is peak relatability, though the premise is well-worn.
pro: His aching knee, unread EMIs and a meeting in ten minutes, while he sits your final exam, is a swap this house already half lives.

title: What If You Could Switch Off Your Emotions for a Day?
con: Fear switching off the night before the exam, then nothing in your grandmother's hug, is this life plus a true decision-science turn.
pro: Turns a relatable pre-exam wish into a devastating emotional and neurological trap backed by Damasio's decision-making research.

title: What If You Could Never Feel Pain?
con: A proven curiosity with a shocking real syndrome and a guilt-driven personal cost.
pro: A superpower-turned-curse backed by shocking real SCN9A cases, and a genuine reframe of what pain is for.

title: What If You Were Paid in Hours of Your Life?
con: The father's remaining balance is moving, but the title is abstract and the conceit echoes In Time.
pro: It turns salary anxiety and a father's working life into one potent visual metaphor with exceptional Indian resonance.

title: What If Nobody Could Tell a Lie Within 10 Feet of You?
con: A funny, escalating truth-aura with a strong partner scene, though the title is long and it echoes Liar Liar.
pro: A 10-foot truth radius is a brilliant visual device for 2D animation that turns from office comedy into a claustrophobic trap in a small bedroom.

title: What If You Could Never Feel Fear Again?
con: A fearless interview, a highway, and a hospital bed give the month a shape, with a sibling hurt while you feel nothing.
pro: Reframes daily anxiety as protection with a barely-known, cinematic real case at its core.

title: What If You Felt Everyone's Pain?
con: A packed commute makes radical empathy physically immediate, with the hospital abandonment providing a sharp moral reversal.
pro: The packed-train opening and mirror-touch science are strong, and abandoning a hospitalised friend is a real cost.

title: What If ₹100 Appeared in Your Account Every Second?
con: A hundred rupees a second ticking on the bus is irresistible until the freeze lands on your parents' home loan.
pro: Free money triggering a bank freeze that swallows your parents' savings is dread every UPI user feels.

title: What If You Could Only Speak 100 Words a Day?
con: A counter that burns one word at a time, with a crying friend and nine left, is built for this kind of animation.
pro: A scarcity constraint that turns every conversation into visible tension and matches the pause-time format.

title: What If Your AI Double Survived You?
con: The grieving mother hook is moving, but starting with 'you' already dead undermines the channel's second-person lived-experience engine.
pro: The funeral phone call is an instant tap and deadbots are urgently, factually real right now.

title: What If Your Face Committed a Crime?
con: Reads more like a standard cyber-thriller plot than a personal what-if rule that subverts a human wish.
pro: Deepfake CCTV plus the real $25M Hong Kong case makes 'your face did it' terrifyingly plausible.

title: What If You Had 60 Seconds With Your Past Self?
con: One minute through a door to the you doing homework stages cleanly and runs on a familiar kind of regret.
pro: An evergreen younger-self prompt dramatised by a hard 60-second constraint and a misfire ending.

title: What If You Only Needed 2 Hours of Sleep?
con: Extra waking life is appealing and relatable, but loneliness must carry the middle once productivity consequences are established.
pro: Directly rebutts hustle culture with a strange genetic fact and a lonely, earned cost.

title: What If You Lived a Second Life Every Night?
con: By month three you are grieving someone your waking partner has never met, which is a life splitting in two.
pro: Two-way dream conversations are a great fact; identity-blur arc is solid but familiar.

title: What If Every Database Forgot You?
con: Aadhaar-era dread is real and the 850 million fact lands, but it is colder than the forgotten-by-mother version.
pro: Viscerally captures modern urban India's reliance on digital IDs and UPI with strong family medical stakes, despite slightly dry title phrasing.

title: What If Every Lie Showed on Your Skin?
con: The lie about already eating, written along your forearm for the metro and then your father to read, draws itself.
pro: Visible text is ideal for the animation style and turns tiny family lies into accumulating public and private consequences.

title: What If You Could Unsay One Sentence a Day?
con: Captures a tender dinner-table regret, but the mechanic of unsaying words while your mother's face retains the hurt is logically muddled.
pro: This is intimate and visually elegant, but its quiet emotional scale demands exceptionally precise writing to retain viewers.

title: What If You Spoke Every Language Tonight?
con: The parents' private language is a lovely Indian-household beat, but the title is flat and the premise is thin.
pro: Code-switching Indian homes make the bus a wonder and the kitchen a betrayal; viewers stay for the translated sentence.

title: What If You Got Your Lifetime Salary Today?
con: Compelling payday hook, though savvy viewers will note that a lump sum invested in index funds or bonds outpaces inflation rather than sitting idle.
pro: The balance-screen hook is excellent and inflation adds substance, though the story needs more than gradually dwindling money.

title: What If Your Dreams Went Live?
con: A spicy viral-shame hook, but the science is thin and it overlaps the stronger search-history idea.
pro: Merges livestream culture with the fear of being judged for thoughts you didn't choose; build is the stretch.

title: What If You Grew One Centimeter a Day?
con: Good built-in escalation and square-cube science, but it leans body horror and constant re-rigging.
pro: Square-cube law is a good boggle, but the daily-growth stakes escalate slowly.

title: What If You Met the You Who Stayed?
con: A rich road-not-taken theme, but the title is cryptic and won't earn the tap.
pro: The defining fork of this age, with both versions able to lose the parent, room or each other.

title: What If Your Dreams Were Someone Else's Real Life?
con: A haunting daughter-who-vanishes idea, but it is distant from the viewer's life and needs a whole second world.
pro: Its eerie opening and disappearing dream-family promise retention, though the factual insight is less novel than the fiction.

title: What If You Saw Your Future, But Couldn't Change It?
con: A phone video of you crying with happiness in a year can nag, and the block-universe gloss stays a seminar.
pro: The self-fulfilling future supplies a strong mystery engine, but block-universe exposition could overwhelm the human story.

title: What If You Could Switch Off Gravity for Yourself?
con: A fun metro float, but bone loss is a slow-motion payoff and it duplicates the other gravity idea.
pro: The oldest fantasy turned into body-horror with a real lesson and clean animation potential.

title: What If Your Shadow Was Living Your Other Life?
con: A shadow detaching at 3am is pure paper-cut, and quantum branching does not cash the life you followed it into.
pro: The detached shadow is visually native to this channel and gives alternate-life regret a strong cinematic device.

title: What If You Could Speak Every Language on Earth Fluently?
con: It turns into a generic powerful-people thriller, and the wish is not an everyday one.
pro: The vanishing-dialect vendor is moving, but it duplicates M32 and skews less domestic.

title: What If You Could Sell Your Sleep?
con: Sleep-selling is relatable but the arc (sell, crash) is linear and the science is familiar.
pro: A marketplace frame makes the invisible sleep cost literal and exam-relatable.

title: What If Gravity Stopped Pulling You?
con: The orbital-physics reveal is strong, but the premise overlaps the other gravity idea and quickly leaves relatable human life behind.
pro: The 30 km/s reveal is a genuine mind-boggle, though the emotional stakes arrive late.

title: What If You Stopped Aging at 25, and No One Else Did?
con: A familiar immortality trope presented only as a sparse stub without a concrete six-minute dramatic engine.
pro: A vanity wish with a brutal mother-keeps-ageing cost and a genuinely strange longevity boggle.

title: What If AI Took Your Job, and Everyone Else's?
con: Feels like a generic macroeconomics news explainer on AI automation rather than an intimate, rule-driven Say Suppose story.
pro: A live anxiety with a strong premise, but the boggle is thin until a deeper fact is sourced.

title: What If Your Dog Could Tell You What Hurts?
con: A disjointed stub that pivots abruptly from an aging pet to crow mask experiments without a cohesive narrative arc.
pro: A tender pet daydream with a real animal-cognition boggle, but the stakes stay small.

title: What If You Were Invisible for a Day?
con: A classic premise reduced to a one-line physics gotcha with almost no story engine.
pro: A classic fantasy with a clever physics gotcha, but the emotional arc needs a stronger person.

title: What If You Got Paid Every Month for Nothing? (universal basic income)
con: Reads like an economics explainer with a parenthetical title, and has no personal story engine.
pro: A clean UBI daydream but the boggle and personal stakes need deepening to carry a full film.

title: What If All Money Vanished Overnight?
con: An incomplete stub with no human character at all and a trivial observation that most modern money is digital.
pro: A strong abstract boggle but it lacks a personal engine to hold a 6+ minute felt story.

title: What If Your Clone Was Born Today?
con: A baby handed over as you spends the whole idea in that one correction.
pro: A tidy misconception-buster but the emotional engine is modest until the clone's divergence is dramatised.

title: What If You Could Breathe Underwater, and He Couldn't?
con: A confusing pronoun in the title, elementary-school oxygen trivia, and a one-line story stub make this unworkable.
pro: A strong sibling-danger hook, but the boggle is small and the world stays at the pool.

title: What If the Moon Vanished Tonight?
con: Terrace chai under an empty moon stays a sky fact about smaller tides.
pro: A neat physics correction but the personal stakes are thin without a stronger human thread.

title: What If You Won the Lottery Tomorrow?
con: A done-to-death premise with a mild finding and no real stakes or escalation.
pro: Busts a real myth but the daydream is common and the felt stakes are low.
